statement: A straight line commensurable with the side of a rational plus a medial area is itself also the side of a rational plus a medial area.
heath_proof: Let AB be the side of a rational plus a medial area, and let CD be commensurable with AB; it is to be proved that CD is also the side of a rational plus a medial area. Let AB be divided into its straight lines at E; therefore AE, EB are straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial, but the rectangle contained by them rational. [X. 40] Let the same construction be made as before. We can then prove similarly that CF, FD are incommensurable in square, and the sum of the squares on AE, EB is commensurable with the sum of the squares on CF, FD, and the rectangle AE, EB with the rectangle CF, FD; so that the sum of the squares on CF, FD is also medial, and the rectangle CF, FD rational. Therefore CD is the side of a rational plus a medial area.

10.69
**Statement:** A straight line commensurable with the side of a rational plus a medial area is itself also the side of a rational plus a medial area.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the side of a rational plus a medial area, and let CD be commensurable in length with AB. We must show that CD is also the side of a rational plus a medial area.

**Step 2.** Since AB is the side of a rational plus a medial area, let it be divided into its component straight lines at E, so that AE and EB are two straight lines incommensurable in square, the sum of the squares on AE and EB is medial, and the rectangle contained by AE and EB is rational [10.40]. By 10.46, this division point E is unique.

**Step 3.** Since CD is commensurable in length with AB, let CD be divided at F such that CF is to FD as AE is to EB [6.12]. Then since AE is to EB as CF is to FD, we have AE is to CF as EB is to FD [5.16, alternando]. But AB is commensurable in length with CD, and AB is the sum AE + EB while CD is the sum CF + FD. Since AE : CF = EB : FD and AE + EB is commensurable in length with CF + FD, it follows that AE is commensurable in length with CF, and EB is commensurable in length with FD [10.11].

**Step 4.** Since AE is commensurable in length with CF, the square on AE is commensurable with the square on CF [10.11, by the duplicate ratio, since commensurable in length implies commensurable in square]. Likewise, since EB is commensurable in length with FD, the square on EB is commensurable with the square on FD. Therefore the sum of the squares on AE and EB is commensurable with the sum of the squares on CF and FD [10.15, applied to the commensurable pairs and then combined via 10.12].

**Step 5.** But the sum of the squares on AE and EB is medial [by hypothesis from 10.40]. Since the sum of the squares on CF and FD is commensurable with a medial area, it is itself medial [10.23 applied to areas: a medial area is one incommensurable with the rational square, and an area commensurable with a medial area remains incommensurable with the rational square by 10.13, hence is medial by D10.1.4].

**Step 6.** Since AE is commensurable in length with CF and EB is commensurable in length with FD, the rectangle AE by EB is commensurable with the rectangle CF by FD [6.16, 10.11]. But the rectangle AE by EB is rational [by hypothesis from 10.40]. Therefore the rectangle CF by FD is commensurable with a rational area, and hence is itself rational [D10.1.4].

**Step 7.** Now we must show that CF and FD are incommensurable in square. Since AE and EB are incommensurable in square, the square on AE is incommensurable with the square on EB. But the square on AE is commensurable with the square on CF (since AE is commensurable in length with CF), and the square on EB is commensurable with the square on FD (since EB is commensurable in length with FD). Therefore by 10.13, since the square on AE is incommensurable with the square on EB, and the square on AE is commensurable with the square on CF, the square on CF is incommensurable with the square on EB. And since the square on EB is commensurable with the square on FD, the square on CF is incommensurable with the square on FD [10.13 again]. Hence CF and FD are incommensurable in square.

**Step 8.** We have established that CF and FD are incommensurable in square, the sum of the squares on CF and FD is medial, and the rectangle CF by FD is rational. Therefore by the definition given in 10.40, the whole CD = CF + FD is the side of a rational plus a medial area. Q.E.D.
